context: Checkpoint 2026-08-02 (night). The debts are paid before the lane grows. `refarm agent finish --lane before-push` now runs the three repo-wide gates that existed only in CI — validate-packages, task:build-order:check, and the high-severity audit — each proven by breaking it on purpose and watching the lane refuse with the failing step named. They join before-push and no earlier lane because each asks a whole-repo question, and none compiles anything. The audit is blocking, matching CI rather than softening it; auditConfig.ignoreGhsas is the escape hatch and it charges a written reason. The tidy.test.ts 'failures' were not a defect: the test pinned one of the two spellings createPackageScriptCommand produces, so its verdict depended on the directory vitest was launched from — green under turbo forever, red from the repo root. It now pins the rule and passes from either. Earlier the same day: twelve defects surfaced by the first push in six days (three real product defects, two unfed CI registries, two security highs, four stale assertions), plus the operator's field bug — farm-start "<id>" dropped the operation id to an indexOf(-1), fixed, tested and republished to ~/.refarm/dist/farm-client. CI is green.
